title: Nighthawks
videoFormat: Photoreal cinematic story film built from the painting's four characters, plus a step-inside flythrough
hook: The painter is in here. Twice.
caption:
The painter is in this painting. Twice.

Hopper finished Nighthawks on January 21, 1942, about six weeks after Pearl Harbor. Swipe for the details: a diner with no way in, a five-cent cigar sign, the notes where his wife Jo turned the customers into "night hawks", and the line she wrote the next day that explains who really posed at that counter.

The Art Institute of Chicago bought it within four months for $3,000. Now it's one of the most parodied paintings in the world.

Save this for your next visit to Chicago, then watch the reel: we brought all four of them to life.

notes: CTA phone uses assets/hopper/nighthawks_shot10_start_1080.png (photoreal film still), not the flythrough frame. Painting is likely still in copyright in some places (Hopper d. 1967), so we use only our existing scan and crops of it, and no other Hopper works. Period photos are PD (OWI/LoC, WPA/NYPL via Wikimedia Commons). The 'two men' Hopper posed for is from Jo's letter; we don't say which figures, though 'the two men' most naturally means the two male customers. Slide 3 dimout photo is Sept 1942, after the painting; copy is framed as the year's mood, not the painting's source.
